articles.summary: Mega-Sena 3074 sorteou as seis dezenas que podem pagar o prêmio acumulado de R$ 227 milhões para quem acertar o resultado deste sábado.
articles.body:
O sorteio do concurso 3.074 da Mega-Sena foi realizado na noite deste sábado (24), em São Paulo. O prêmio para as apostas que acertassem as seis dezenas era de R$ 227.660.457,38 milhões .

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet, até as 20h – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Os jogos podem ser realizados até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A Mega tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, quintas e domingos .

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e o tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: 2º turno: Quaest divulga última pesquisa de intenção de voto para governador do RN; veja números | G1
articles.standfirst: A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos.
articles.summary: A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos.
articles.body:
No Rio Grande do Norte, de acordo com a Quaest, Allyson, do União Brasil, e Cadu de Lula, do PT, estão tecnicamente empatados na margem de erro, um dia antes da eleição. O levantamento foi contratado pela Inter TV Cabugi. A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos.

Allyson, do União Brasil, tinha 45% das intenções de voto na primeira rodada. Agora, continua com 45%. Pela margem de erro, tem de 43% a 47%. Cadu de Lula, do PT, tinha 42% na primeira rodada. Agora, tem 44%. Pela margem de erro, tem de 42% a 46%. Segundo a Quaest, os dois candidatos estão tecnicamente empatados na margem de erro. Indecisos somam 3%. Votos em branco ou nulos são 8%.

A pesquisa da Quaest com os votos válidos para o Rio Grande do Norte. Allyson, do União Brasil, tem 51%. Considerando a margem de erro, pode ter de 49% a 53%. Cadu de Lula, do PT, 49%. Pela margem, de 47% a 51%. Allyson e Cadu de Lula estão tecnicamente empatados dentro da margem de erro.

A Quaest ouviu 2.154 eleitores em 62 cidades, sexta-feira (23) e sábado (24).

articles.title: Kim Jong-un encerra visita à China em gesto de aproximação com Pequim | G1
articles.standfirst: Líder norte-coreano esteve na cidade chinesa de Dandong, na fronteira entre os dois países, visitou memorial da Guerra da Coreia e atravessou ponte recém-inaugurada, vista como símbolo da aproximação comercial.
articles.summary: Líder norte-coreano esteve na cidade chinesa de Dandong, na fronteira entre os dois países, visitou memorial da Guerra da Coreia e atravessou ponte recém-inaugurada.
articles.body:
O líder norte-coreano, Kim Jong-un, deposita uma coroa de flores durante visita ao Memorial da Guerra para Resistir à Agressão dos EUA e Ajudar a Coreia, em Dandong, na província de Liaoning, China, em 24 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: KCNA via REUTERS

O líder da Coreia do Norte, Kim Jong-un , voltou ao país por via terrestre neste sábado (24), pelo horário de Brasília — já domingo (25) na Ásia —, após visitar um importante memorial da Guerra da Coreia na cidade chinesa de Dandong, na fronteira entre os dois países. A informação foi divulgada pela imprensa estatal norte-coreana.

Kim atravessou uma ponte recém-inaugurada que liga a Coreia do Norte à China , seu principal parceiro comercial. O gesto foi visto como um símbolo do esforço de Pequim e Pyongyang para ampliar os laços comerciais.

A imprensa estatal da Coreia do Norte deu grande destaque ao peso histórico da visita e descreveu a relação entre os dois países como um vínculo “inquebrável”, construído durante o conflito de 1950 a 1953.

Durante o tour, Kim afirmou que o povo norte-coreano vai “lembrar para sempre os anos gloriosos de luta ao lado do povo chinês” e transmitir de geração em geração a “gratidão ao povo chinês, que ajudou nossa revolução com sangue”, segundo a agência estatal KCNA.

A visita é interpretada como um novo movimento de China e Coreia do Norte para fortalecer a relação econômica antes da viagem do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, à região no próximo mês.

O episódio também evidencia o esforço diplomático de Pyongyang para equilibrar relações, enquanto aprofunda seus laços militares com Moscou nos últimos dois anos.

O líder norte-coreano, Kim Jong-un, caminha ao lado de Wang Huning, presidente do Comitê Nacional da Conferência Consultiva Política do Povo Chinês (CPPCC, na sigla em inglês), pela Nova Ponte do Rio Yalu, que liga Dandong, na China, a Sinuiju, na Coreia do Norte, durante visita à cidade chinesa, na província de Liaoning, em 24 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: KCNA via REUTERS

A última visita de Kim a Pequim havia sido em setembro de 2025, para um desfile militar. Já o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, esteve na Coreia do Norte em junho.

Segundo a KCNA, ao observar a nova ponte do ponto central da travessia, Kim afirmou esperar que a estrutura “cumpra corretamente sua missão histórica de ligar os dois países e unir firmemente o sentimento dos povos das duas nações”.

As duas Coreias seguem tecnicamente em guerra, já que o conflito de 1950 a 1953 terminou com um armistício, e não com um tratado de paz.

articles.title: Arquidiocese de NY: Vítimas de abuso aprovam acordo de US$ 800 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Indenização encerra processos movidos por cerca de 1.300 pessoas. Acordo evita falência da instituição e prevê a liberação de documentos sobre agressores
articles.summary: A Arquidiocese de Nova York indenizará 1.300 vítimas de abuso sexual em acordo que prevê a abertura de arquivos sigilosos sobre agressores.
articles.body:
Sobreviventes de abusos sexuais cometidos por membros da Igreja Católica aprovaram um acordo de US$ 800 milhões (cerca de R$ 3,9 bilhões) com a Arquidiocese de Nova York.

Segundo os advogados das vítimas informaram neste sábado (24), o valor vai encerrar processos movidos por aproximadamente 1.300 pessoas.

A arquidiocese católica havia concordado com o pagamento em maio.

Esta é uma das maiores indenizações em uma onda de ações judiciais sobre abuso sexual contra a Igreja nos Estados Unidos.

O valor fica atrás apenas de um acordo de US$ 880 milhões firmado pela Arquidiocese de Los Angeles, também em 2024.

O escritório de advocacia Jeff Anderson & Associates, que representa 300 dos sobreviventes, classificou a decisão como "um momento poderoso na busca por justiça".

Além do pagamento de US$ 800 milhões, a arquidiocese concordou em liberar documentos relacionados aos agressores sexuais dentro da Igreja.

O acordo evita que a Arquidiocese de Nova York declare falência, mas permite que os sobreviventes continuem processando as seguradoras da Igreja em busca de indenizações adicionais, segundo a agência Reuters.

Nos últimos anos, a Igreja Católica pagou bilhões de dólares em acordos por todos os Estados Unidos.

A onda de reparações financeiras ocorreu após Nova York e outros estados americanos aprovarem leis que permitiram, de forma temporária, que vítimas de abuso sexual infantil abrissem processos civis por crimes cometidos há décadas, driblando os prazos de prescrição tradicionais.

articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada neste sábado (24) é a última antes do 2º turno, neste domingo, e foi encomendada pela Rede Amazônica.
articles.summary: Pesquisa Quaest para o governo do Amazonas aponta Omar Aziz com 59% dos votos válidos e Maria do Carmo com 41% na véspera do segundo turno.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada neste sábado (24), véspera do 2º turno, mostra como está a disputa pelo governo do Amazonas. Nos votos válidos, Omar Aziz ( PSD ) tem 59% das intenções de voto, contra 41% da Professora Maria do Carmo ( PL ).

É a forma como o TSE divulga o resultado oficial das eleições. São os votos dados nos candidatos. Esse cálculo deixa de fora os votos em branco e nulos e as abstenções. Para vencer no 2º turno, um candidato precisa de 50% dos votos válidos mais um voto.

Nas pesquisas, as empresas excluem os votos em branco e nulos e os eleitores indecisos para calcular os votos válidos.

Para estimar os votos válidos, a Quaest leva em consideração as intenções de voto e o perfil de comparecimento. É o modelo likely voter, que considera eleitores com maior propensão a votar .

O levantamento foi encomendado pela Rede Amazônica e ouviu 2.154 eleitores de 16 anos ou mais, entre os dias 23 e 24 de outubro de 2026. A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa foi registrada na Justiça Eleitoral sob o número AM-09902/2026.

Esses resultados ajudam a medir o grau de consolidação do voto. Quanto maior o número de indecisos na véspera, menos consolidado está o voto e maior a possibilidade de mudanças em relação ao resultado de domingo.

articles.title: Judge who awarded 36 death sentences in 16 months transferred to family court
articles.summary: UP judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar, who handed down 36 death sentences in 16 months, transferred from Muzaffarnagar fast-track court to family court.
articles.body: MUZAFFARNAGAR: Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar, who made national headlines for awarding 23 death sentences in 11 cases between April and Sept this year in Muzaffarnagar and 13 in Bareilly, has been transferred from fast track court to family court, according to a judicial transfer order. He will now take charge as additional principal judge of the family court in Muzaffarnagar.TOI had on Aug 17 reported about Judge Diwakar’s string of death sentences. The jurist was transferred to Muzaffarnagar on Nov 29, 2025. As a presiding officer of fast track court-3, he heard criminal cases involving Muzaffarnagar and Shamli districts. On Sept 7, he pronounced his 23rd death sentence in Muzaffarnagar court, convicting a man for burning his wife alive.His tenure drew attention when at least 97 pending case files involving murder and other serious offences were recalled from his court in Aug on the orders of the then-district and sessions judge Birendra Kumar Singh. Singh has since retired.Diwakar subsequently questioned the basis for recalling the cases. In a NDPS case judgment, he touched upon the matter, observing that it was not merely whether such files could be taken back on administrative grounds, but also the “reasons behind exercising that power”. Further, he questioned the “absence of recorded reasons”.In May 2022, as a civil judge (senior division) in Varanasi, Diwakar ordered a court-monitored videographic survey of the Gyanvapi mosque complex in a case concerning the worship rights of five Hindu women at the Shringar Gauri site.During the survey, a structure in the ‘wuzu khana’ area was claimed by Hindu petitioners to be a Shivling, a claim disputed by the Muslim side. The Supreme Court subsequently transferred the proceedings to the Varanasi district judge’s court.Following the order, Diwakar reported receiving threats, prompting authorities to review his security. In 2024, he again raised “threat” concerns from “international phone numbers”.More recently, during his Muzaffarnagar posting, the judge questioned changes to his security arrangements. In a communication to UP DGP, he stated that the removal of his assigned gunner had “compromised his protection”.Police, however, maintained that alternative personnel had been deployed. Diwakar, 46, joined the Uttar Pradesh judicial service as a Munsif/civil judge (junior division) in 2009. He holds B.Com, LL.B and LL.M degrees. His earlier postings included Azamgarh, Sultanpur, Budaun and Varanasi.He served as civil judge (senior division) in Varanasi from April 2021 to July 2022, before moving to Bareilly, where he later became an additional district and sessions judge (fast track court). He was posted in Chitrakoot from April to Nov 2025 and joined Muzaffarnagar in Nov 2025, as per official records.According to the latest judicial order, Shiv Kumari, the presiding officer of fast track court-2 and additional sessions judge, has now been moved to fast track court-3.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Agra | Silver Rate in Agra | Bank Holidays in Agra | Public Holidays in Agra | Agra AQI | Weather in Agra | Petrol Price in Agra | Diesel Price in Agra | CNG Price in Agra | LPG Price in AgraStay updated with the latest Agra news. articles.title: Nearly 1,000 arrested in French protests marred by 'elevated' violence: minister
articles.summary: French police arrested "nearly 1,000" people Saturday in nationwide protests in which officers were confronted with "an extremely elevated level of violence"...
articles.body:
French police arrested "nearly 1,000" people Saturday in nationwide protests in which officers were confronted with "an extremely elevated level of violence" from black-clad extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.

Although marches over the cost of living "passed off well" in cities, "ultra-left" groups took to throwing projectiles and aiming fireworks at police to provoke clashes, he told journalists.

Two people were "seriously injured", he said: one in the city of Toulouse, where a 20-year-old man reportedly had fingers blown off, and the other in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case.

Nunez compared Saturday's figures with those from a week ago, when a first round of national demonstrations over the cost of living degenerated into street violence, with hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people ending up being arrested.

He said that the nearly 1,000 arrests recorded on Saturday compared with the same time a week ago, when authorities had recorded 385 arrests.

He also said that, while some shops and businesses had been vandalised and looted on Saturday, "the scale was far smaller" than a week earlier, and he stressed that shopping centres had been well protected this time.

In Paris, where the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully but clashes broke out with police as the crowd dispersed, Nunez said "several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the march, including around 500 individuals identified as rioters".

Ensuing clashes in the capital lasted for around two hours, he said.

The minister said that in the southern cities of Cannes and Montpellier, authorities "for the first time" saw far-right activists who sought confrontations with "ultra-left militants" or who claimed to be there to protect businesses.

Overall, Nunez said, Saturday's outcome appeared more "positive" than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses.

The authorities would remain "on high alert" through the night and into Sunday, he said.

articles.summary: Kai Cenat’s fallout with former friend Reggie has moved beyond social media arguments, with a reported cease-and-desist letter raising the stakes in their
articles.body: Kai Cenat’s fallout with former friend Reggie has moved beyond social media arguments, with a reported cease-and-desist letter raising the stakes in their public dispute. The legal move comes after weeks of controversy over serious allegations involving the popular streamer. Kai’s legal team has denied the claims and demanded that Reggie remove related posts and videos. Reggie, however, appears ready to fight back, publicly discussing the legal notice and releasing a music video that seems to draw inspiration from their ongoing conflict.Kai Cenat’s cease-and-desist letter targets Reggie’s allegationsAccording to TMZ, Kai Cenat’s legal team sent Reggie a cease-and-desist letter dated October 2, accusing him of making false and misleading statements online. The letter reportedly demands that Reggie stop repeating the disputed claims and remove social media content connected to them.Kai’s representatives strongly rejected allegations that he engaged in pedophilia or exchanged sexual favors for opportunities on his platform.“We want to be unequivocal: the suggestion that Mr. Cenat has ever engaged in any form of pedophilia, or exchanged s*x for platforming any person, is categorically false,” the statement read.The letter reportedly argues that Reggie has not supplied evidence to support his claims. Kai’s attorney also described the allegations as “nonsense” and said they had harmed the streamer’s reputation and business relationships.The document reportedly raises additional concerns about alleged threats against Kai and people associated with him. According to the letter, the situation has created safety concerns for employees and disrupted business operations.However, a cease-and-desist letter is a legal demand, not a court ruling. The allegations and denials remain distinct from any finding of legal responsibility.Reggie responds to Kai Cenat’s legal move with a music videoReggie has shown little sign of stepping away from the dispute publicly. Before news of the reported legal action emerged, he shared what he described as court documents on Instagram and suggested he was prepared to involve his lawyers.“Finally finna call my lawyers rn!!”He later addressed the cease-and-desist in an Instagram Story, writing, “Kai Ceant sent a cease and desist but he never addressed the pdf stuff lol ok ‘watch me.’”Reggie has also released a YouTube music video for his track ‘Watch Me!’ Its visuals appear to reference the moment he was served with legal papers near the AMP House. The video also mentions Kai’s clothing brand, VIVET, and fellow streamer RaKai, bringing the dispute into his music.The developments have sparked divided reactions online. Some social media users have praised Kai’s decision to seek legal action, while others have questioned the move or argued that the claims should be examined in court.For now, the dispute remains unresolved. articles.title: A Czech man found a stone in his garden in 2007; archaeologists later identified it as a 3,350-year-old Bronze Age spearhead mould
articles.summary: A stone that once formed part of a barn’s foundations in the Czech Republic has turned out to be a rare Bronze Age tool used to cast bronze spearheads.
articles.body: A stone that once formed part of a barn’s foundations in the Czech Republic has turned out to be a rare Bronze Age tool used to cast bronze spearheads. Discovered in 2007 in the village of Morkůvky in South Moravia, the rectangular slab was later identified as a casting mould from the Late Bronze Age. The find is about 3,350 years old. Archaeologist Milan Salaš of the Moravian Museum in Brno led the research, which was published in the peer-reviewed journal Archeologické rozhledy in 2025. The mould’s carefully preserved impression reveals the shape of the weapon it produced, while analysis of the stone indicates that it had travelled a considerable distance from its geological source in what is now Hungary. The find offers a glimpse into Bronze Age metalworking and the movement of materials across Central Europe.How a stone in a Czech barn was identified as a Bronze Age artefactThe mould was discovered in 2007 in Morkůvky, a village in the Břeclav District of South Moravia. According to the research published in Archeologické rozhled titled A unique stone mould for casting a spearhead from Morkůvky in South Moravia as an example of long-distance import in the Urnfield Period, and its technological contribution, the object is a well-preserved half of a stone casting mould. It measures about 23 centimetres in length and is made from rhyolite tuff, a volcanic rock. The stone was found in a garden, where it was sticking slightly out of the ground near the foundations of an old barn. Its significance became clear only after archaeologists examined it. Salaš described it to Radio Prague International as a regular rectangular slab with a precisely shaped impression on one side of the surface where the two halves of the mould would meet.The research team used macroscopic examination and X-ray fluorescence (XRF) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses to investigate the object and traces left by the casting process. The results indicated that bronze had been poured into two halves positioned upright and held together with copper wire. The analyses also helped researchers investigate the material associated with the casting process. The mould is particularly informative because the impression left inside it remains sufficiently clear to identify the type of weapon it was designed to produce. Although the artefact was found outside a documented archaeological excavation, its shape, manufacturing technology and raw material provide evidence about Bronze Age craftsmanship and exchange.What the spearhead mould reveals about Bronze Age tradeThe impression in the stone shows that it was used to cast a socketed, lance-shaped spearhead. The blade had longitudinal ribs along its wings and central midrib, while the socket featured a sharp ridge. The socket was designed to receive the end of a shaft, allowing the finished bronze head to be attached to a spear. According to the study, spearheads of this type are commonly found in the Carpathian Basin and are generally associated with the Late Bronze Age. The form therefore offered an important clue to the mould’s origins. Researchers then used petrographic analysis, which examines the mineral and structural characteristics of rocks, to investigate where the stone came from.Their findings identified the material as rhyolite tuff, with its geological source traced to a region extending from northern Hungary towards southeastern Slovakia. The geological evidence, combined with the spearhead’s distribution, led the researchers to conclude that the mould had been brought to South Moravia from the Carpathian region during the Bronze Age. Researchers believe it was probably brought to the village in modern times from a nearby archaeological site associated with the Urnfield culture. The geological evidence points to the stone’s origin in the Carpathian region, while researchers believe the mould was later moved to Morkůvky from a nearby Urnfield site. The discovery provides evidence of connections between the Carpathian region and communities associated with the Middle Danube Urnfield culture. The Urnfield culture takes its name from the practice of burying cremated remains in urns and was widespread across parts of Central Europe during the Late Bronze Age. Researchers believe it was probably brought to the village in modern times from a nearby archaeological site associated with the Urnfield culture.What the mould tells researchers about Bronze Age weapon productionThe stone also preserves evidence of how it was used. The study describes visible traces of scorching and heat damage, including changes to the rock around the mould’s impression. These marks are consistent with repeated exposure to the high temperatures involved in casting molten bronze. The researchers’ examination of the mould’s construction and wear provides insight into the practical process of making a spearhead. The two halves were positioned vertically and secured together with copper wire before the molten metal was poured in. A core was also used to form the hollow socket into which the weapon’s shaft would later fit.Unlike a finished spearhead, which shows the shape and design of a weapon, a casting mould offers evidence of the manufacturing process itself. It can reveal how a metal object was formed and how the craftspeople who made it worked with stone, metal and heat. The mould’s clear impression and traces of intensive heating make it useful for studying prehistoric metalworking technology. The research was published in 2025, about 18 years after the stone was discovered. Its identification transformed an unremarkable piece of a barn’s foundations into evidence of Bronze Age craftsmanship and long-distance exchange. The mould now helps researchers understand how spearheads were made and how materials and technological traditions moved across Central Europe about 3,350 years ago.You use AI every day. articles.title: Protests sweep France, Spain as masked mobs loot shops, clash with cops; 1,100 held
articles.summary: Anti-establishment demonstrations turned violent in France and Spain on Saturday, with protesters clashing with police, shops being looted and public
articles.body: Anti-establishment demonstrations turned violent in France and Spain on Saturday, with protesters clashing with police, shops being looted and public property damaged.Authorities in Barcelona arrested 100 people after hooded demonstrators vandalised stores, while French police made nearly 1,000 arrests during protests over the cost of living and school funding.In Barcelona, demonstrators taking part in a rally against the establishment set fire to street furniture and looted shops around the central Plaza de Catalunya, an area popular with tourists and weekend shoppers.Catalonia's interior minister, Núria Parlon, said around a quarter of those arrested in Barcelona were minors. More than 30 fires were set and 14 shops were vandalised or looted, she added.The demonstrations were promoted on social media as a movement "against the system". Posts also used the slogan "Institut Indignats", a translation of "Lyceés Indignés", the name used by students who have protested in France in recent weeks. Both phrases refer to indignant or dissatisfied high school students.Videos shared online showed people trapped inside shops, including the department store El Corte Ingles, after shutters were lowered to prevent looting. Other footage showed hooded demonstrators dressed in black smashing shop windows and taking goods, sometimes encouraged by people watching online.Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni warned that acts of vandalism "will not go unpunished". He also said the guardians of minors involved could face legal consequences.Tear gas and clashes in French citiesIn France, clashes broke out in Paris and several other cities as demonstrations against rising living costs and school funding drew hundreds of thousands of people. The protests, described by organisers as an “Acte II”, or second round, came a week after unrest involving widespread looting and damage to public buildings.The interior ministry estimated that 410,000 people took part nationwide, including 110,000 in Paris. The CGT union, which helped organise the demonstrations, put the national turnout at nearly 800,000 and the Paris crowd at 250,000. The ministry said turnout was lower than the 550,000 people it estimated had protested the previous weekend.The main Paris march began peacefully but descended into clashes near its endpoint in the east of the city. articles.title: O que considerar antes de escolher os materiais para o banheiro  | G1
articles.standfirst: Da distribuição do espaço aos acabamentos, algumas decisões precisam ser tomadas antes de iniciar a reforma.
articles.summary: Da distribuição do espaço aos acabamentos, algumas decisões precisam ser tomadas antes de iniciar a reforma.
articles.body:
O banheiro reúne diferentes funções em poucos metros quadrados. Bancada, área de banho, bacia sanitária e espaços de circulação precisam funcionar em conjunto, o que torna o planejamento uma etapa importante antes mesmo de escolher cores, formatos ou acabamentos. Uma peça que chama atenção na loja pode não ter as dimensões ou características adequadas para o espaço disponível.

O primeiro passo é partir das medidas reais do ambiente. A abertura de portas e gavetas, as distâncias entre os elementos e o espaço necessário para circulação interferem diretamente na distribuição. Na bancada, por exemplo, a definição da cuba influencia altura, profundidade e área livre para apoio. Já a posição da bacia sanitária deve considerar os pontos hidráulicos existentes e o espaço necessário para uma utilização confortável.

As dimensões da cuba e da bancada devem ser avaliadas em conjunto para preservar espaço de apoio e circulação no banheiro — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

A Cuba de Apoio Redonda Slim , da Deca, é um exemplo de como proporção e instalação precisam entrar na decisão. Com 40 centímetros de diâmetro, o modelo de apoio ocupa uma posição de destaque sobre a bancada e exige que a altura e a profundidade sejam planejadas considerando a peça. Antes da compra, portanto, vale observar não apenas o desenho, mas também sua relação com o móvel, o metal e a área disponível ao redor.

A área de banho exige outra análise. Por receber água diretamente, ela pede materiais compatíveis com essa condição e atenção à superfície do piso, ao caimento e à quantidade de juntas. Nas paredes, formato e paginação também interferem tanto no resultado visual quanto na rotina de conservação. Placas maiores podem diminuir a presença de rejuntes, enquanto diferentes tipos de superfície exigem cuidados específicos de limpeza.

Formato, paginação e características da superfície devem ser considerados de acordo com o local onde o revestimento será aplicado — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

O Calacata Oro 90x90, da Biancogres , inspirado no mármore de fundo claro e veios marcados, mostra como a escolha do revestimento também precisa considerar o conjunto. Antes de definir sua aplicação, é importante conferir o acabamento da versão escolhida e a indicação de uso do fabricante, além de planejar recortes e paginação. Assim, a estética passa a caminhar junto com as necessidades técnicas de cada área.

A escolha da bacia sanitária também precisa considerar mais do que o desenho. Dimensões, formato, tipo de instalação e posição dos pontos hidráulicos interferem na circulação e na organização do banheiro. Em ambientes menores, alguns centímetros podem fazer diferença na passagem entre bancada, área de banho e demais elementos.

Outro ponto que merece atenção é o que acontece depois da reforma. Quantidade de rejuntes, acesso aos cantos para limpeza, encontro entre bancada e cuba e facilidade de conservação das superfícies fazem parte da rotina do banheiro. Pensar nesses aspectos ainda durante o planejamento pode evitar soluções bonitas na entrega, mas pouco práticas no uso diário.

Na Vilarejo, comparar as peças fisicamente permite observar dimensões, acabamentos e combinações antes da definição. Com as medidas do banheiro em mãos, também fica mais fácil analisar quais produtos fazem sentido para cada aplicação e como cuba, bacia sanitária, metais e revestimentos irão se relacionar dentro do mesmo ambiente.

Um banheiro bem resolvido não depende de uma peça isolada. Ele começa quando medidas, circulação, instalações e materiais são pensados em conjunto. A aparência continua fazendo parte da escolha, mas divide espaço com decisões que determinam como aquele ambiente será utilizado todos os dias.

articles.title: Leandro Grass: trajetória do candidato ao segundo turno no DF | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato pelo PT é adversário da governadora Celina Leão. Eleição ocorre neste domingo (25) até 17h.
articles.summary: Leandro Grass (PT) disputa o segundo turno contra Celina Leão (PP) após o TSE confirmar nova votação para o governo do Distrito Federal em 25 de outubro.
articles.body:
Leandro Grass (PT), candidato ao GDF em 2026 — Foto: Globo/Ueslei Costa

O candidato ao governo do Distrito Federal Leandro Grass (PT) chega ao 2º turno neste domingo (25) tentando inverter o placar registrado na primeira rodada de votação, no início do mês.

Se conseguir, Grass devolverá o PT ao comando do Palácio do Buriti após um jejum de 12 anos – desde o fim do governo Agnelo Queiroz (PT), em 2014.

O candidato disputa a vaga com a atual governadora e candidata à reeleição Celina Leão (PP), que recebeu 49,93% dos votos válidos. Já o candidato do PT ficou em segundo lugar, com 34,47%.

Essa é a segunda eleição de Grass, que foi candidato ao governo em 2022. Na ocasião, foi derrotado no primeiro turno pelo então candidato à reeleição Ibaneis Rocha (MDB).

Além do DF, cinco estados terão disputa em segundo turno : Espírito Santo, Amazonas, Rio Grande do Norte, Acre e Tocantins.

A campanha de Grass, nos dois turnos, se concentrou nas críticas ao governo Celina Leão e em cobranças sobre a crise do BRB e a crise na saúde pública da capital.

O candidato se apresentou como uma oportunidade de mudança e afirmou que um eventual governo dele "não seria de esquerda, mas do povo".

Ao longo do primeiro turno, Grass se juntou aos demais candidatos de direita e de esquerda para formar uma "aliança tácita" e fazer frente à candidatura de reeleição. Em debates e sabatinas, os candidatos evitaram ataques mútuos e concentraram a artilharia nos problemas do governo atual.

No segundo turno, o candidato também procurou ampliar a frente política em torno da chapa. Grass recebeu o apoio de Ricardo Cappelli e do PSB, além da mobilização de deputados distritais de esquerda.

Grass também contou com o "apoio não declarado" de José Roberto Arruda. Após se tornar inelegível, o candidato do PSD continuou fazendo críticas ao governo de Celina Leão e indiretamente ajudou a campanha petista.

A campanha ainda contou com a participação do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva em uma caminhada em Ceilândia. Nas ruas, Grass apostou em uma agenda com panfletagens, atos, passeatas e encontros com moradores.

Nascido em Brasília , Leandro Grass, 41 anos, foi criado no Guará, onde viveu a infância e parte da juventude.

O candidato é formado em Sociologia pela Universidade de Brasília ( UnB ) e possui mestrado em Desenvolvimento Sustentável pela mesma instituição, além de formação em Gestão Cultural pela Organização dos Estados Ibero-Americanos (OEI).

Professor, pesquisador e gestor público, ele construiu sua trajetória profissional ligada à educação, participação social e formulação de políticas públicas.

A entrada na política ocorreu em 2018, quando foi eleito deputado distrital pelo Rede.

Leandro Grass, candidato ao governo do DF — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Durante o mandato na Câmara Legislativa, foi autor de 27 leis. Entre as iniciativas aprovadas estão a criação de espaço exclusivo para mulheres no BRT Sul, a reserva de vagas de trabalho para mulheres vítimas de violência e a proibição de sacolas plásticas .

Essa é a segunda candidatura de Grass para o governo. Em 2022, ele era representante do PV ficou em segundo lugar no pleito com 434 mil votos, equivalente a 26,25% do total – foi derrotado em primeiro turno por Ibaneis Rocha, que conquistou a reeleição.

Após a posse do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, em 2022, foi escolhido para presidir o Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional (Iphan). Permaneceu no cargo até março de 2026.

O estado todo também está sob alerta amarelo, que significa "perigo potencial" para temporais.

New Delhi reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir remains an integral and inalienable part of India and demanded that Pakistan vacate all territories under its illegal occupation.Speaking at an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Minority Issues at the UN General Assembly's Third Committee, India's First Secretary at the Permanent Mission to the UN, Raghoo Puri, called out Pakistan's conduct and said its representatives should focus on the welfare of their own people instead of taking directions from the military."Pakistan predictably misused the forum for propaganda. Jammu & Kashmir is an integral and inalienable part of India. Pakistan must vacate the territory under its illegal occupation," Puri said.He further said Pakistani representatives would do well to look inwards and address the concerns of their own citizens rather than act on military directives.India slams Pakistan over minority rightsPuri underlined that protecting minority rights was primarily the sovereign responsibility of individual states, guided by the principle of sovereign equality.He said India's civilisational tradition of diversity was reflected in its constitutional safeguards for religious and linguistic minorities. He also highlighted the substantial contributions made by minorities to India's national development, including at the highest levels of government and key institutions.The latest confrontation followed India's strong rebuke to Pakistan at the UN on October 23 over its treatment of religious minorities. New Delhi accused Islamabad of failing to protect vulnerable communities while attempting to lecture India on religious freedom, burial rights and minority protections.During an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Religion or Belief, India's First Secretary at the UN mission, Bhavika Mangalanandan, challenged the report's approach to religious discrimination during the Covid-19 pandemic and its advocacy concerning funeral rights for terrorists.Mangalanandan argued that the report appeared to place disproportionate emphasis on discriminatory practices and shortcomings in countries in the Global South while overlooking similar tragedies in developed nations.India asserts climate justice and judicial independenceSeparately, India also defended its approach to climate change at the UN General Assembly, stressing the importance of equity, climate justice and sustainable development.Deputy secretary Barkha Tamrakar delivered India's statement before the Third Committee on the report of the Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers, titled “An urgent and existential threat: the role of justice systems in addressing the climate crisis.”Tamrakar described climate change as a serious global challenge with consequences for development, livelihoods and human rights. She said India's response was guided by equity, climate justice, sustainable development and the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC).She highlighted the Constitution, environmental legislation, the National Green Tribunal and an independent judiciary as key safeguards supporting environmental protection in India.Tamrakar also noted that the Supreme Court had recognised the fundamental rights to life and equality as essential protections against the adverse effects of climate change.On judicial independence, she pointed to transparent, institutionally supervised training programmes, including those conducted by the National Judicial Academy, as measures to strengthen impartiality and safeguard the independence of the judiciary.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Saddam Hussein opened a cheesecake factory’: Obama’s jibe at Trump’s White House
articles.summary: Former US President Barack Obama took a dig at Donald Trump over his renovation plans for the White House, saying Trump has \"got the White House looking
articles.body: Former US President Barack Obama took a dig at Donald Trump over his renovation plans for the White House, saying Trump has "got the White House looking like former Iraq President Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory".Obama made the remarks while campaigning for the midterm elections in Ohio. He mocked Trump’s changes to the White House, saying the president appeared more interested in renovations than other matters."I don't know if you've noticed, but he seems very focused on home renovations. He should be on HGTV. The guy’s building a ballroom that’s bigger than the White House. Paved over the Rose Garden, put a helicopter pad on the South Lawn, and there’s gold everywhere! What’s up with the gold? Everything—more gold!” Obama said.He continued his criticism, drawing laughter and applause from the crowd. “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. Just gold everywhere."After his speech, Obama took to social media platform X to urge voters to support Democratic candidates in Ohio’s gubernatorial and Senate elections."Ohio, let's do what we can to elect Amy Acton as your next Governor and Sherrod Brown as your next US Senator! They’ve dedicated their lives to fighting on behalf of all Ohioans," Obama wrote.Obama also stressed the importance of grassroots campaigning and high voter turnout, saying collective action could help bring about positive change in the country."If we’re willing to organise and mobilise, if we’re willing to turn out in big numbers in Ohio and across this country, if we’re willing to vote for change and vote for Democrats up and down the ballot, then this election might just mark the moment this country began moving in a better direction," he stated.He ended his message by urging voters to make sure they cast their ballots.Obama targets Pete HegsethObama also criticised US defence secretary Pete Hegseth, linking the ongoing conflict with Iran to concerns over the country's military preparedness."Hundreds of Americans have been wounded. We have run down our stock of missiles, and Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, you’ve got the defense secretary who’s squarely focused on important matters like the jawlines and testosterone levels of our troops," he said.What are US midterm electionsUS midterm elections take place every four years, halfway through a president’s four-year term. They are seen as an important test of public opinion on the president and the ruling party.The elections determine control of Congress, with all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and roughly one-third of the Senate seats up for election. The results can influence the president’s ability to pass laws and implement policies.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Yindjibarndi native title payout: Fortescue's A$150.3 million award faces three appeals
articles.summary: Native title compensation in Western Australia reached a record level when the Federal Court ordered Fortescue to pay the Yindjibarndi people A$150.3
articles.body: Native title compensation in Western Australia reached a record level when the Federal Court ordered Fortescue to pay the Yindjibarndi people A$150.3 million for mining their Pilbara country without agreement. The award, the largest in Australian history, covers cultural and economic loss at the Solomon Hub iron ore operation, which began production in 2013 on land where the Yindjibarndi hold exclusive native title. The Yindjibarndi Ngurra Aboriginal Corporation had originally sought A$1.8 billion, and the gap between that figure and the final orders has left traditional owners, lawyers and Indigenous leaders questioning how economic loss is valued under current law.Court awards A$150 million for cultural loss after 124 spiritually significant sites destroyedJustice Stephen Burley's judgment rested largely on cultural loss, according to ABC, which reported that the A$150 million award reflects the destruction of at least 124 spiritually significant sites. Solomon Hub covers around 135 square kilometres of Yindjibarndi land. Final orders made on 1 July 2026 added A$136,757 for economic loss and A$217,152 in compound interest on that economic amount, the Yindjibarndi Ngurra Aboriginal Corporation said in a media release.The case was only the third native title compensation claim the Federal Court has decided. It was preceded by a 2019 payout of A$2.5 million to the Ngaliwurru and Nungali peoples and a A$54 million award in February 2026, as per reports.Why the economic loss award fell far short of the claim; freehold land value and Timber CreekThe Yindjibarndi Ngurra Aboriginal Corporation launched its claim in 2022, seeking A$1 billion for cultural damage, A$678 million for economic loss, A$34.85 million for the destruction of sites and A$112.13 million for social disharmony, The Guardian reported. The economic award came to a small fraction of what was sought because the court valued the loss using freehold land value, following the 2019 High Court decision at Timber Creek in the Northern Territory, the case behind the earlier payout to the Ngaliwurru and Nungali peoples.The corporation had argued for a benchmark based on the royalties that mining companies pay under native title agreements in the region. Chief executive Michael Woodley told the media in a statement that the headline amount was unsatisfactory given what has been lost. The mine has generated an estimated A$80 billion in revenue since operations began, yet it was approved by the Western Australian government without the permission of the traditional owners.Fortescue and the Western Australian government argued for far lower compensation figuresFortescue sought to cap compensation at about A$8 million, while the Western Australian government argued that between A$5 million and A$10 million would be appropriate. After the judgment, the company said it would review the court's reasons once they were available.Executive chair Andrew Forrest told Guardian Australia that Fortescue has always accepted fair and proper compensation for the Yindjibarndi people and pays traditional owners across the Pilbara under seven native title agreements. "We will pay the compensation tomorrow if given the opportunity," he said.Woodley told the media he was disappointed that the Western Australian government sided with the mining company. He said the state could have stayed neutral on the amount and left the other parties to argue it out in court.Yindjibarndi people lodge appeal after unanimous vote, targeting cultural and economic rulingsNative title holders voted unanimously to appeal at a large meeting in Roebourne on 30 July 2026, the corporation said in the same release. The meeting lasted several hours, and legal representatives advised members on the available appeal pathways before every attendee, in person and online, voted in favour. Woodley told the media in the release that members had decided "the only option was to keep fighting".The corporation lodged its appeal in late August, ABC reported. Woodley had told the media that its lawyers would challenge both the cultural loss and economic loss rulings. A successful appeal could push the compensation figure closer to the original claim, using what the corporation describes as an industry-standard royalty rate. The corporation also intends to renew its argument that Fortescue systematically divided the Yindjibarndi people by funding a breakaway native title group and harmed their ability to practise traditional ceremonies.The release also noted that Fortescue has mined Yindjibarndi land since 2012 without an Indigenous Land Use Agreement or any other agreement with the corporation, which is the registered native title body corporate. The mine is expected to operate until 2045. Under current legislation, Fortescue does not have to consult the corporation or obtain its agreement while its activities stay within existing mining leases.Western Australian government and Fortescue file their own appeals as legal fight widensThe Western Australian government lodged its own appeal in quick succession. Documents filed with the Federal Court show that it follows similar grounds to the state's original case. It disputes nearly every dimension of Justice Burley's judgment and calls the cultural loss award "manifestly excessive". The State Solicitor's office wrote that the judge failed to give adequate reasons for a sum nearly three times the February award to Northern Territory traditional owners. Attorney-General Tony Buti told the media at the time that the appeal sought clarity on the law, although one critic accused the government of trying to appear business friendly.Fortescue then became the third party to appeal, filing a cross-appeal. A company spokesperson told ABC that it restates positions put forward at trial and seeks clarity on aspects of the judgment that the company believes are inconsistent with existing legal principles and precedent. The spokesperson said Fortescue felt forced to respond to the other two appeals to protect its legal position. The spokesperson added that paying the full award within 24 hours, so the money reached the Yindjibarndi community quickly, had not ended the matter.Woodley told the media in a statement that both appeals were disappointing, even if consistent with the positions held during the case. He said the Yindjibarndi people expect any company working on their country to respect Yindjibarndi laws. A date for the appeals to be heard has not been set.Native title lawyers and commentators call for reform as the ruling sets a precedentNational Native Title Council chair Kado Muir told the media in May that the compensation formula is flawed, saying the economic figure "wouldn't buy you a front porch". Native title lawyer Greg McIntyre, who worked on the Mabo case, told the same outlet that the decision is a watershed likely to be followed in Western Australia, Queensland and other mining regions. He said it shows native title carries a value tied to spiritual connection, not just real estate.Resources journalist Paul Cleary, author of the book Title Fight, told the broadcaster that the corporation should appeal and that legislation needs reform. He argued the state should be accountable for approving mining licences where companies have no agreement with native title holders. Under the Western Australian Mining Act, compensation liability passes to the tenement holder once the state approves a tenement. Justice Burley affirmed that position, leaving the state government without financial consequence.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US asylum gamble blew gangster Himanshu Bhau’s cover: 'Used fake passport to evade global law'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A gamble to secure asylum in North America may have blown the cover of gangster Himanshu Bhau, one of north India’s notorious fugitives.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A gamble to secure asylum in North America may have blown the cover of gangster Himanshu Bhau, one of north India’s notorious fugitives.A day after TOI reported his detention in Nevada, sources said a brief, staged detention in Feb by Bhau and his aide Neeraj Faridpuria, designed to exploit legal loopholes and claim asylum, backfired and unravelled the plan.The two face more than 25 criminal cases each across Delhi, Haryana and Punjab, including murder. Once the duo deliberately surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and details were fed into US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tracking system, which set off red flags.‘Bhau used fake passport to evade global law’Sources said fugitives from India were aggressively seeking this modus operandi. Lawrence Bishnoi’s brother, Anmol, too had tried it but was busted.Currently lodged at the Henderson Detention Center under the jurisdiction of ICE, Bhau, sources said, used a forged passport under the alias Himanshu Singroha and evaded global law enforcement for over four years.However, his calculated scheme to get himself deliberately detained along with his chief associate, Neeraj Faridpuria, who also was using a fake passport under the name Neeraj Kaushik, triggered their detention.Once the duo deliberat-ely surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and personal details were fed into the ICE track-ing system. Picking up critical leads from this database entry, Indian law enforcement agencies and US security counterparts dug deeper into the background of “Himanshu Singroha”.Through cross-verification with local intelligen-ce sources, police contacts, and diplomatic counterparts, authorities confirmed that the individual in custody was indeed the high-profile fu­gitive Himanshu Bhau, a source said.The details on the ICE portal, accessed by TOI, corroborate the details, including the fake name on the passport. Investigations further revealed Faridpuria also shifted his base from Portugal to the US in late 2025 before reuniting with Bhau.The cops shared a dossier, including a photograph showing Faridpuria with guns and their other biometric details, which confirmed they were using forged documents. They were formally detained and information was shared with Indian agencies.The two are linked to the 2024 murder in South Delhi’s Aya Nagar in which over 70 bullets were fired, another recent connected killing, the 2019 murder of Congress leader Vikas Chaudhary in Faridabad, and a shooting outside YouTuber Elvish Yadav’s residence.Following confirmation of their detention in a Nevada prison, Indian agencies are working with US auth­orities to expedite their deportation. articles.summary: Saudi Arabia's civil defense said on Saturday it intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis towards the Mecca and Medina
articles.body: Saudi Arabia's civil defense said on Saturday it intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis towards the Mecca and Medina regions, with debris falling at multiple locations, including Jeddah, Taif and Rabigh.The Houthis denied targeting the two regions, saying their operations were directed at Saudi oil facilities and military bases. The group added that it announces such attacks when they take place.The latest developments come as the Houthis continue to threaten Saudi Arabia's critical infrastructure. On Sunday, the rebel group's military spokesperson Yahya Saree reiterated that Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport remained a "military target" and warned airlines, airport staff and travellers against using the facility.The warning came hours after the airport announced that Terminal 1 would handle domestic flights and Terminal 2 international flights operated by national carriers from Sunday.Airport operations were suspended on October 10 following an attack claimed by the Houthis that killed 13 people and injured more than 300. The shutdown was extended two days later.The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities with missiles and drones as the conflict widens.Riyadh has also intensified its military involvement in Yemen, launching strikes against the group and supporting a government counteroffensive after the Houthis seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tiger Shroff firing: Turkish, desi pistols recovered in Surat, youth held in MP
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Cops investigating last Sunday's firing at actor Tiger Shroff arrested a 22-year-old student from Indore and recovered a Turkish-made Zigana
articles.body: MUMBAI: Cops investigating last Sunday's firing at actor Tiger Shroff arrested a 22-year-old student from Indore and recovered a Turkish-made Zigana pistol, a country-made firearm and 10 live cartridges from Surat. Pranjal Thakaran, who is pursuing engineering in Haryana's Sonipat, is the 11th suspect to be arrested in the case. He is suspected to be part of the support network and to have been in contact with a shooter, reports Mateen Hafeez.According to investigators, Thakaran's name surfaced during interrogation of the arrested accused and through technical evidence. A Mumbai police officer said his alleged links to the weapon supply chain were being examined.About the recovery of the weapons, sources said Mumbai police had taken the arrested shooters to Surat to find the spot where they had discarded the weapons. It took police around 8-10 hours to locate the firearms. The weapons and ammunition will be sent to the Kalina forensic science lab for ballistic analysis. Police sources say Lawrence Bishnoi gang has used the Zigana pistol in the past.‘MP youth was in contact with shooter who fired at Tiger’The youth arrested from Indore, Pranjal Thakaran, was in contact with the person who allegedly carried out the firing at actor Tiger Shroff, preliminary questioning of the arrested suspects has indicated. However, investigators said his exact role in the conspiracy would be established only after further questioning.Thakaran, who is studying in Haryana, was arrested from a rehab centre in Indore. “Thakaran had arrived in Indore five days ago to meet his brother, who is undergoing treatment in the city,” said additional DCP Rajesh Dandotiya.The arrest followed inputs received by Mumbai Crime Branch about Thakaran’s presence in Indore. Dandotiya said Mumbai Crime Branch contacted its Indore counterparts on Thursday night, following which technical surveillance and other inputs helped trace his location. A joint team subsequently arrested him.Thakaran was produced before an Indore magistrate court, which granted him a three-day transit remand. He will be brought to Mumbai and produced before the Esplanade court for further remand proceedings.The arrest is part of a wider investigation into the Oct 18 firing outside a location in Juhu, where five to six rounds were fired at Shroff’s car. The actor escaped unhurt, while his driver and a vlogger sustained injuries. articles.title: ‘Will never be safe’: Houthis warn as Riyadh airport resumes flights
articles.summary: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh resumed flight operations on Sunday and designated terminals for domestic and international services, hours
articles.body: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh resumed flight operations on Sunday and designated terminals for domestic and international services, hours before Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis renewed their warning against using the “military target”.The airport administration announced that Terminal 1 would handle domestic flights and Terminal 2 international flights operated by national carriers, effective Sunday.“Please be advised that Terminal (1) will be designated for domestic flights and Terminal (2) for international flights operated by national carriers at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, effective Sunday, October 25, 2026,” the airport administration said in a passenger update posted on X late on Saturday.The airport also urged passengers with confirmed bookings to check their flight status with their airlines before travelling to the airport.“We kindly advise passengers with confirmed bookings to contact their airlines to verify the status of their bookings and flights before heading to the airport. We appreciate your cooperation and compliance with the instructions,” the advisory said.Aslo Read: Missile debris fall in Mecca, Medina after Saudi intercept strikes; Houthis deny targeting holy citiesHours later, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said operations targeting the airport would continue and warned airlines, airport staff and travellers against using the facility.“The Yemeni Armed Forces renew their warning to all global, regional, and local airlines, as well as employees and travellers, against traveling through Khalid Airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe, being a military target for our forces,” Saree said in an X post.“The Saudi regime bears the consequences of any operation of the airport and what will result from that, because the Armed Forces will continue their operations toward it and it will never be safe,” he added.Houthis earlier claimed attacks on Saudi airports, energy infrastructureThe latest warning follows earlier claims by the Houthis that they had targeted King Khalid International Airport and several other aviation, military and energy facilities across Saudi Arabia.Saree said the group had targeted locations in Riyadh, Yanbu, Dammam, Rabigh and other areas.“We targeted King Khalid Airport in Riyadh and Aramco Company in Yanbu,” the Houthi spokesperson said.He also claimed attacks on energy infrastructure, saying, “We targeted Rabigh Refinery and the East-West oil pipeline in Saudi Arabia.”Saree further claimed that the group had targeted other aviation and military facilities.“We targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Najran Airport, and Khamis Mushait Airbase,” he said.Air India, Air India Express suspend Saudi flightsAmid the evolving security situation, Air India and Air India Express have suspended flights to and from key destinations in Saudi Arabia.According to the airlines' advisory, services connecting Riyadh and Dammam will remain suspended through November 7, while flights to and from Jeddah will be suspended through October 31.The airlines have offered affected passengers complimentary rebooking options or full refunds.You use AI every day. articles.title: Two cottonmouth snakes were filmed entwined in Alabama water; online commenters said the venomous pair were male rivals fighting, not mating
articles.summary: Cottonmouth snakes intertwined in the water near Birmingham, Alabama, have sparked an online debate over whether the venomous pair were mating or fighting
articles.body: Cottonmouth snakes intertwined in the water near Birmingham, Alabama, have sparked an online debate over whether the venomous pair were mating or fighting over territory. Footage of the pair shared on Reddit's Snakes community shows them entwined yet almost calm, which led the person who posted it to suspect courtship. Fellow snake enthusiasts quickly disagreed in the comments, describing the encounter as a contest between rival males. The clip was recorded just south of the city, and the disagreement over its meaning has turned a strange sighting into a small lesson in telling territorial combat apart from courtship between snakes.Original poster watched the Alabama cottonmouths for ten minutes and found them together an hour laterAccording to The Cool Down, the original poster told Reddit's Snakes community they felt compelled to share the sighting and were fairly certain it was mating, while admitting they might be wrong. That hedge matters, because it left the thread open to correction. The poster later told commenters they had watched the pair for a good ten minutes and that the snakes were not being particularly aggressive with one another.The poster was working nearby at the time. After leaving to carry on with that work and returning about an hour later, they said the two were still together, doing what they could only describe as cuddling.Commenters dispute the mating claim and describe a territorial duel between two male cottonmouthsSoon after the footage appeared, commenters streamed into the thread to challenge the idea that the snakes were mating. The reaction was swift enough that the debate was well under way before the poster added their later observations. One commenter told the original poster the pair were two males in combat, while another told the thread it looked like a "territorial thumb war on water." The second remark is a joke, but it neatly captures the reading that took hold in the thread, a standoff between two rivals rather than a courtship.Reddit users amazed by male combat in water as one predicts a female is waiting to breed with the winnerOther commenters told the thread they were amazed that the territorial display took place in such an unusual location. One said they had never seen male combat in water and urged others to watch their step, because a female would probably be nearby, waiting to breed with the winner of the duel. Another commenter joked that it was possibly the first footage they had seen of naval combat between vipers. The mixture of astonishment and wordplay shows how the footage was received: as an unusual sight worth enjoying as much as analysing.Similar snake fights mistaken for mating were reported at Colorado's Garden of the Gods and in GreecePeople have made the same mix-up elsewhere, The Cool Down noted in May this year, at Colorado's Garden of the Gods, snakes taken to be mating were in fact battling for breeding rights. At Sitia Geopark in Greece, two males fighting over turf looked like an exotic mating ritual. The same article also pointed readers to a different kind of sighting in India, where a king cobra was filmed making an elegant glide along the shoreline.What the Alabama cottonmouth video shows about reading snake behaviour from an online videoThe episode shows how quickly an inaccurate description can be corrected when footage is shared publicly. The poster offered a guess and admitted uncertainty, other users supplied a competing explanation within the same thread, and the poster then added fuller observations of their own. Even though the original account was inaccurate, the pair's calm demeanour explains why the mistake was easy to make.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Watch: IAF's Surya Kiran team paints skies over Varanasi during 'Wings over Ganges'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team took to the skies over Varanasi on Sunday as the holy city hosted ‘Wings over Ganges’, an aerial display at Namo
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team took to the skies over Varanasi on Sunday as the holy city hosted ‘Wings over Ganges’, an aerial display at Namo Ghat marking the 94th Indian Air Force Day celebrations.In the video shared by IAF, red and white aircraft can be seen in skies over the river Ganga.The event is set to feature the IAF’s premier display teams, including the Sarang Helicopter Display Team, alongside a range of military aircraft, including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, Sukhoi-30MKI and Rafale.Aircraft from the Navy and the Army are also expected to participate, highlighting jointness among the three services.Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who represents Varanasi in the Lok Sabha, is scheduled to attend the display as the chief guest during his visit to the city on October 25.Indian Air Force chief AP Singh said the IAF was committed to jointness and integration, adding that future conflicts would be multi-domain and require the three services to operate more closely.“We are not viewing theaterisation as an exercise to permanently divide fighter assets geographically,” Singh told news agency PTI.On the proposed theaterisation of the armed forces, he said the key question was how to employ air power to its greatest effect within an integrated structure.“Future conflicts will be multi-domain by their very nature; three services will operate together far more closely than ever before,” the IAF chief said.During his Varanasi visit, PM Modi is also scheduled to inaugurate a new garment manufacturing facility at Arvind Mills.Preparations are under way across the city to welcome the Prime Minister, with members of Generation Z planning to shower rose petals at multiple points as part of a reception ahead of his visit to his parliamentary constituency.PM Modi is scheduled to travel to Arvind Mills by an Army helicopter after arriving in Varanasi.His roadshow will begin at Police Lines and pass through the Cultural Complex and Chowkaghat before reaching Namo Ghat, where he will attend the ‘Wings over Ganges’ aerial display.

articles.title: Drug trafficking crackdown: Amit Shah hails Operation Trident; Rs 100 crore hawala transactions exposed, 18 arrested
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday announced a major crackdown on an international narcotics cartel, with Operation Trident targeting 38
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday announced a major crackdown on an international narcotics cartel, with Operation Trident targeting 38 locations across Assam, Mizoram and Manipur.The operation, that took place on October 23, uncovered hawala transactions worth Rs 100 crore and resulted in the freezing of 1,424 bank accounts and the attachment of properties valued at Rs 17.82 crore. Officials also seized 500 detonators and Rs 12 lakh in cash, while 18 people were arrested.Announcing the operation on X, Shah said that the cartel was trafficking narcotics across India, Myanmar and Bangladesh through the Death Triangle Corridor. He credited the central agencies and police forces of the three states for the crackdown.“Modi Govt deals another lethal blow against drugs with Operation Trident,” Shah said in his post.He said that the agencies had launched coordinated crackdowns across the three states, dismantling the international network and uncovering its financial transactions. The operation, he added, was part of the Centre's mission to eliminate every drug network in the country by December 31, 2029.“The offensive attests to India’s Himalayan resolve to realise the mission of eradicating every drug network by 31 December 2029. India will hammer until the last nail is driven into the coffin of drug cartels,” Shah said.Congratulating the anti-narcotics team, the home minister acknowledged the role of central agencies and the police forces of Assam, Mizoram and Manipur in the operation.“Heartiest congratulations to the anti-narcotics team comprising central agencies, and police forces of the three states.”Centre targets drug networks by December 2029The operation comes amid the Centre's push to eliminate drug networks from the country by December 31, 2029. Shah has said that the home ministry will dedicate the remaining part of 2026 and the following three years to freeing the country from the drug menace.He has also called on police forces across the country to participate wholeheartedly in implementing the Nasha Mukt Bharat roadmap.At the third National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) heads of states and Union territories in New Delhi in September, Shah said the country would collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade by December 31, 2029.He emphasised coordinated action, clear targets and accountability, along with the need to dismantle drug networks. Protecting young people from substance abuse, he said, was also important to achieving the national vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan reaches over 35 crore peopleThe Centre's anti-drug efforts also include the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, implemented by the ministry of social justice and empowerment under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR).As on date, the campaign has reached more than 35 crore people, including over 13.94 crore young people and 10.86 crore women. It has also engaged with more than 32 lakh educational institutions.Launched on August 15, 2020, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan initially covered 272 vulnerable districts before expanding its reach across the country. The campaign places particular emphasis on young people, women and communities, recognising their role in preventing substance use and promoting healthy lifestyles.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Photos: Clashes erupt in France during protests over rising living costs
articles.summary: Authorities deploy 70,000 officers to combat violence. Nearly 1,000 arrests made.
articles.body:
Clashes have erupted across France as hundreds of thousands of people marched against rising living costs, a week after protests descended into rioting and prompted a tough security response from President Emmanuel Macron’s government.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said police arrested nearly 1,000 people nationwide on Saturday and faced “an extremely elevated level of violence” from black-clad “ultra-left” demonstrators.

Riot police fired tear gas in Paris and other major cities, including Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes as officers moved to disperse crowds and protect shops and public buildings.

Authorities deployed about 70,000 security personnel across the country for the latest demonstrations in a bid to prevent a repeat of the unrest from a week earlier when public buildings were vandalised, hundreds of businesses were looted and 2,700 people were arrested.

Nunez said Saturday’s outcome was more “positive”, citing faster police interventions, more pre-demonstration checks and stronger protection for commercial areas.

At least two people were seriously injured, including a man in Toulouse who reportedly had fingers blown off and another person in Clermont-Ferrand, Nunez said, without giving details.

Despite the government’s claims of an improvement, rights advocates and protesters voiced anger over what they saw as an assault on freedoms and the right to demonstrate, six months before the election to choose Macron’s successor.

[Hannah McKay/Reuters]
Hundreds of thousands of people across France marched on October 24, 2026, in a second wave of protests against deteriorating school conditions and the rising cost of living. [Abdul Saboor/Reuters]

France’s Ministry of the Interior said 410,000 people protested nationwide, including 110,000 in Paris. The CGT, one of France’s largest union confederations, put both figures at nearly double the official totals. [Hannah McKay/Reuters]
People attend a demonstration against "racism, fascism and imperialism" as the far-right National Rally party holds its congress in Orleans, France. [Stephanie Lecocq/Reuters]
Authorities said 500 “rioters” clashed with law enforcement agents, but the level of violence was not comparable to confrontations during protests last weekend. [Jeremias Gonzalez/AP Photo]

A protester at an authorised demonstration organised by a labour union in Marseille holds a French flag reading, "We are the future of France," on a monument dedicated to French reserves and militia who died during the Franco-Prussian War. [Manon Cruz/Reuters]

articles.title: Man arrested for extortion plot
articles.summary: Urwa police in Mangaluru arrested 42-year-old Naveen Thoras for an alleged extortion conspiracy; booked under BNS, remanded to judicial custody.
articles.body: Mangaluru: Urwa police have arrested a 42-year-old man in connection with a case involving an alleged conspiracy to extort money and property by making false allegations, including an accusation of murder, against a woman and publicly tarnishing her family’s reputation.City police commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy stated that the accused, Naveen Thoras, a resident of Shaktinagar, Mangaluru, was arrested on Friday based on evidence gathered during the investigation.According to police, the case was registered at Urwa police station on Aug 10, following a complaint by a woman, who alleged that a conspiracy had been hatched to extort money and property from her by making false allegations of a serious crime and damaging her family’s reputation in public.A case was registered under Sections 61(a)(1) and 308(7) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The accused was produced before a court on Saturday and remanded to judicial custody. Police said the investigation is continuing and that further action would be taken after a detailed probe into the alleged involvement of other accused in the case.Stay updated with the latest Mangaluru news.
